message:
fix(update): there was no moment when the update became final

Wiring registration to the shared unit turned up a real bug, and the test that
found it is the one that mattered: roll back after a failed health check and
check the files went back.

They did not. RegisterInstall deleted the .gnlink-old backups as soon as
registration succeeded -- but the order is Register, Relaunch, Health, and
either of the last two can still fail into a rollback. By the time a rollback
ran there was nothing left to restore.

The missing idea was a point at which the update becomes final. Commit() is
that point, and the state machine calls it only from Done and from
UpdatedButNotRelaunched, which are the two endings that do not roll back.
Everything before them keeps the way back.

An old assertion had been holding the bug in place -- "backups are dropped only
after registration" was true, which is why the bug passed. It now says the
opposite, because the opposite is what has to be true.

The registration wiring itself builds capture, apply and restore together,
sharing one snapshot, because they only make sense as a set. The snapshot is
taken before a single file moves: taking it later would capture the state the
update is creating, and rolling back to that would leave the previous build's
files claiming to be the new version -- the same poisoning that ruled out
re-running the old installer. Restoring without having captured reports success
rather than failure; there was nothing to put back, and calling that a failure
would turn an ordinary rollback into RollbackFailed, which is reserved for
installs that may actually be inconsistent.

Two corrections to how earlier work should be described. Skipping an archive
format removes compression and extraction handling; it does not remove the
manifest's name and URL attack surface, which is what the payload-name rules
and the URL policy are for. And the effects suite's check count is verification
of part of the OS path, not evidence that a multi-file update works -- it still
copies one blob to several names.

Tested against a scratch HKCU key with netsh, the SCM and the Start menu
recorded rather than performed. Afterwards the real uninstall key still reads
0.2.104 and the three live PIDs are unchanged.

qwinsta: console active, rdp-tcp listening. 571 checks across the eight suites.
